name: Aminophylline
executiveSummary: Methylxanthine. Adult: load **5–6 mg/kg** slow IV; maintenance **0.5–0.7 mg/kg/h**. Pediatrics load **7 mg/kg**; maint. **0.4–0.8 mg/kg/h** by age. Neonatal apnea: load **5 mg/kg**; maint. **2.5 mg/kg every 12 h** (**5 mg/kg/day**).
indications:
## Indications

- Apnea of prematurity (alternative/adjunct to caffeine per center).
- Bronchospasm / diaphragmatic support in selected regimens.

## Precautions

- Narrow therapeutic window: tachycardia, vomiting, seizures.
- Interactions: ↑ levels with macrolides/quinolones; ↓ with rifampin/phenobarbital/phenytoin.

> Titrate with serum levels when available.

adulto.presentation: Ampule 24 mg/mL (aminophylline ≈ theophylline equivalent per monograph).
adulto.dose: Load **5–6 mg/kg IV** over 20–30 min; maintenance **0.5–0.7 mg/kg/h** continuous IV.
adulto.administration: Slow IV / pump; preferably dilute in NS or D5W (usual conc. **1 mg/mL**, max **25 mg/mL**).

pediatrico.dose: IV load: **7 mg/kg** over 20–30 min. Maintenance: **1–6 months 0.4 mg/kg/h**; **6–12 months 0.6 mg/kg/h**; **1–9 years 0.8 mg/kg/h**; **≥10 years 0.7 mg/kg/h**.
pediatrico.notes: Neonatal apnea: see neonatal profile. Monitor levels.

neonatal.dose: Neonatal apnea: load **5 mg/kg IV** over 20–30 min; maintenance **2.5 mg/kg/dose every 12 h** (**5 mg/kg/day**) — adjust with levels (common target **3–10 µg/mL**).
neonatal.administration: IV via pump; dilute NS/D5W (usual conc. 1 mg/mL).

stability:
## Stability

- Opened ampule: discard remainder. Dilutions: follow local guide (~24 h).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Irritability, tachycardia, arrhythmias, vomiting, seizures, hypokalemia (with β-agonists).

bibliography.citation: AAP. Apnea of prematurity medication context.
